skill.name: Simple, compound or complex?
skill.why: Use only one sentence shape and writing plods. Mix all three!
skill.how: One clause: simple. Two equal clauses: compound. A clause that can't stand alone: complex.

beats.say: Spot the doer and the action.
That chunk is a clause. Just one? It's a simple sentence.
Glue two clauses with and, but or or. Now it's compound.
beats.show: The slime bubbled, **and** Mo ran for the door.

beats.say: Start a clause with when or because. It can't stand alone now.
beats.show: **When I added vinegar**, the slime bubbled.

beats.say: Add a clause like that, and the sentence is complex.

weDo.text: The lights went out, and everyone screamed.
weDo.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
weDo.hint: Count the clauses. Could each part stand alone as a sentence?
weDo.success: Compound. 'The lights went out' and 'everyone screamed' could each be a sentence, and the word 'and' joins them.

options.reason: Two doers each have a verb: the lights went out, everyone screamed. A simple sentence has one clause.
Both parts could stand alone. Complex needs a part that can't stand alone, like one starting with because or when.

weDo.text: We stayed inside because it was hailing.
weDo.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
weDo.hint: Could 'because it was hailing' be a sentence on its own?
weDo.success: Complex. 'Because it was hailing' can't stand alone. It needs 'we stayed inside', the part that can stand alone.

options.reason: Because doesn't join two equals. 'Because it was hailing' can't stand on its own, so this isn't compound.
There are two clauses here: we stayed inside, and it was hailing. Simple has only one.

creature.name: Quillby
creature.blurb: An echidna whose quills are pen nibs, each one writing a single clause, so it can tell a simple, compound or complex sentence just by counting quills.

encounters.frame: Quillby has scratched a sentence into the sand with one quill.
encounters.text: The wombat dug under the fence and into the garden.
encounters.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
encounters.success: Simple. 'Under the fence and into the garden' just says where. There's one doer and one verb: the wombat dug.

options.reason: 'And' joins two places here. Is there a second doer with a verb of its own?
Complex needs a part that starts with a word like because or when. There isn't one here.

encounters.frame: Tully is reading out the footy report, as usual.
encounters.text: Jai kicked a goal, but the umpire blew the whistle first.
encounters.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
encounters.success: Compound. But joins two clauses that could each be a sentence on their own.

options.reason: There are two clauses here: Jai kicked a goal, and the umpire blew the whistle. Simple has only one.
Both halves could stand alone as sentences. Complex needs a part that can't stand alone.

encounters.frame: Mo's recipe cards fell on the floor. Quillby is stacking them into piles.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to the right pile.
encounters.success: Simple sentences have one clause. Compound sentences join two clauses with words like and or but.

items.text: Mo burnt the toast.
items.reason: One doer and one verb: Mo burnt. That's one clause, so it's simple.

items.text: Mo burnt the toast, and the smoke alarm went off.
items.reason: Two clauses, 'Mo burnt the toast' and 'the smoke alarm went off', joined by and.

items.text: The pancake and the jam stuck to the ceiling.
items.reason: 'And' joins two things, the pancake and the jam. There's one verb, stuck, so one clause.

items.text: The pancake flipped, but it never came down.
items.reason: Two clauses joined by but. Each one could be a sentence on its own.

encounters.frame: Quillby wants a compound sentence for the haunted house sign.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to make a compound sentence.
encounters.success: And joins two clauses that could each be a sentence, so it's compound.

accept: The door creaked open, and a bat flew out.
body.reason: Compound needs two clauses that can each stand alone. Could 'because a bat flew out' stand alone?

encounters.frame: Zed wants his game diary to use a compound sentence here.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word that makes this complex, then choose one that makes it compound.
encounters.success: But joins two equal clauses. 'Zed reached the castle' and 'he had no lives left' can both stand alone.

parts.reason: Castle is a thing, not a joining word. Look for the word that links the two clauses.
Lives isn't a joining word. Look for the word that links the two clauses.

options.reason: Even though still starts a part that can't stand alone, so the sentence stays complex.
Because also starts a part that can't stand alone, so it's still complex. It changes the meaning too.

encounters.frame: A message from the space station pops up on Quillby's screen.
encounters.text: When the rocket landed, the crowd cheered.
encounters.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
encounters.success: Complex. 'When the rocket landed' can't stand alone. It needs 'the crowd cheered', which can.

options.reason: Compound joins two clauses that can each stand alone. 'When the rocket landed' can't stand alone.
There are two clauses: the rocket landed, and the crowd cheered. Simple has only one.

encounters.frame: Quillby is reading the skipper's logbook from yesterday's boat trip.
encounters.text: Dolphins and seals were swimming beside our boat.
encounters.prompt: What kind of sentence is this?
encounters.success: Simple. 'Dolphins and seals' is one doer, and 'were swimming' is one verb, so there's one clause.

options.reason: And here joins two animals, not two clauses. There's still only one verb: were swimming.
There's no part starting with a word like because or when, and only one clause anyway.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is live-streaming a concert. He says this sentence is compound because it has 'and'. Is he right?
encounters.text: Although the drums and guitars were far too loud, the crowd loved every song.
encounters.prompt: What kind of sentence is it really?
encounters.success: Complex. 'Although the drums and guitars were far too loud' can't stand alone, so Maxx is wrong again.

options.reason: 'And' joins the drums and the guitars, not two clauses. Could the first part stand alone?
Count the verbs: were, loved. Each has its own doer, so there are two clauses.

encounters.frame: Mo's joke book has three sentences. Quillby only wants the compound one.
encounters.prompt: Tap the compound sentence.
encounters.success: 'Nobody laughed' and 'Mo laughed for five whole minutes' can each stand alone, and 'but' joins them.

parts.tap: Mo's pizza joke was short but very cheesy.
parts.reason: 'But' joins two describing words here, not two clauses. There's only one verb: was.

parts.tap: Nobody laughed, but Mo laughed for five whole minutes.
Because of the cheesy joke, Gus groaned.
parts.reason: 'Because of the cheesy joke' has no verb, so it's a phrase. There's only one clause.

encounters.frame: Wren's rescue diary pages are everywhere. Quillby is sorting them into piles.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to the right pile.
encounters.success: Simple has one clause, compound joins two equals, and complex has a part that can't stand alone.

items.text: Because of the cold, the joey slept in a pillowcase.
items.reason: 'Because of the cold' has no verb, so it's a phrase. The only clause is 'the joey slept'.

items.text: The possum bit my finger, and I yelled.
items.reason: Two clauses that could each stand alone, joined by and.

items.text: Because the echidna was cold, we wrapped it in a towel.
items.reason: 'Because the echidna was cold' can't stand alone, so this is complex.

items.text: The lizard was tiny, but it was very angry.
items.reason: Two clauses joined by but. Each one could be a sentence.

items.text: When the vet arrived, the wallaby hid under the bed.
items.reason: 'When the vet arrived' leaves you waiting. It needs the part that can stand alone, so this is complex.

encounters.frame: Gus's robot has fallen to bits. Quillby has the pieces of its last message.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to make a complex sentence.
encounters.success: 'Because its battery ran out' has a doer and a verb, but it can't stand alone. That makes it complex.

accept: The robot shut down because its battery ran out.
body.reason: Complex needs a clause that can't stand alone. Does 'a flat battery' have a doer and a verb?

encounters.frame: Tully's season report has the wrong joining word. He wants a compound sentence here.
encounters.prompt: Tap the joining word that's wrong. Then choose one that fixes the meaning and makes the sentence compound.
encounters.success: But joins two equal clauses and shows the contrast: they trained hard, and they still lost.

parts.reason: Trained is fine. Look for the word that joins the two clauses.
Season is fine. Look for the word that joins the two clauses.
Lost is fine. Look for the word that joins the two clauses.

options.reason: Although fits the meaning. Could 'although we still lost the final' stand alone as a sentence?
Or gives a choice between two things. Tully isn't offering a choice.

encounters.frame: Quillby is checking captions for the space museum. Only one should be simple.
encounters.prompt: Which of these is a simple sentence?
encounters.success: 'After the launch' has no verb, so it's a phrase. The only clause is 'the astronauts floated around the cabin'.

options.text: After the launch, the astronauts floated around the cabin.
After the rocket launched, the astronauts floated around the cabin.
options.reason: 'After the rocket launched' has its own doer and verb, but can't stand alone. That makes the sentence complex.

options.text: The rocket launched, and the astronauts floated around the cabin.
options.reason: Two clauses that could each stand alone are joined by and. That's compound.

options.text: The astronauts floated around the cabin while the rocket climbed.
options.reason: 'While the rocket climbed' is a clause that can't stand alone, so this is complex.

encounters.frame: Gus's lab report has a sentence Quillby can't quite label.
encounters.text: Because of the smell, Gus wore a peg on his nose for the whole experiment.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best description of this sentence?
encounters.success: Simple. 'Because of the smell' has no verb, so it's a phrase. The only clause is 'Gus wore a peg'.

options.text: simple: it has only one clause
complex: 'because of the smell' is a part that can't stand alone
options.reason: 'Because of the smell' has no verb of its own, so it's a phrase, not a clause.
Because never joins two equals, and there's only one doer and verb here: Gus wore.

options.text: complex: 'for the whole experiment' is a part that can't stand alone
options.reason: 'For the whole experiment' has no verb, so it's a phrase, not a clause.

encounters.frame: Indi is labelling the gallery signs. Each one needs the right sticker from Quillby.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to the right sticker.
encounters.success: Look at what follows before or during. A doer and verb make a clause. No verb? A phrase.

items.text: Before the gallery opened, Indi repainted the whole wall.
items.reason: 'Before the gallery opened' has its own doer and verb, but it can't stand alone. That makes it complex.

items.text: Before lunch, Indi repainted the whole wall.
items.reason: 'Before lunch' has no verb, so it's a phrase. The only clause is 'Indi repainted the whole wall'.

items.text: Indi repainted the wall, but the paint was still wet at the opening.
items.reason: Two clauses that could each stand alone, joined by but.

items.text: The giant prawn sculpture wobbled during the speeches.
items.reason: 'During the speeches' has no verb. The only clause is 'the sculpture wobbled'.

items.text: The prawn wobbled until it fell on the mayor's foot.
items.reason: 'Until it fell on the mayor's foot' has a doer and verb but can't stand alone, so it's complex.

items.text: Indi mopped up the paint, and Mo ate all the snacks.
items.reason: Two equal clauses, 'Indi mopped up the paint' and 'Mo ate all the snacks', joined by and.

encounters.frame: The reef ranger's report has four sentences. Quillby needs the complex one for its collection.
encounters.prompt: Tap the complex sentence.
encounters.success: 'Just as we gave up' has a doer and verb, but can't stand alone. So it's complex.

parts.tap: The reef was quiet this morning.
parts.reason: One clause: the reef was quiet. That's simple.

parts.tap: A turtle and two rays drifted past the boat.
parts.reason: 'A turtle and two rays' is one doer with one verb, drifted. That's still simple.

parts.tap: The divers waited for an hour, but the shark never came.
parts.reason: Two clauses that could each stand alone, joined by but. That's compound.

parts.tap: Just as we gave up, a huge grouper swam under the boat.

encounters.frame: Mo is writing up the bake-off results. Quillby has the pieces.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to make a complex sentence.
encounters.success: 'Even though Mo had baked it for an hour' can't stand alone, so the sentence is complex.

tiles: Mo had baked it for an hour.
accept: The pie was still frozen even though Mo had baked it for an hour.
body.reason: Complex needs a clause that can't stand alone. Which tile makes the baking part unable to stand alone?

encounters.frame: Zed wants the first line of his ghost story to be a complex sentence.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word to change, then choose the replacement that makes the sentence complex.
encounters.success: As soon as turns 'the ghost drifted through the wall' into a part that can't stand alone. Now it's complex.

parts.reason: Flickered is the verb in the first clause. Change the word that joins the clauses.
Drifted is the verb in the second clause. Change the word that joins the clauses.
Wall is fine. Change the word that joins the clauses.

options.reason: But still joins two equal clauses, so the sentence stays compound.
Or joins two equal clauses too, so it stays compound. It doesn't make sense here either.
Then just says what happened next. It doesn't make either clause depend on the other, so the sentence isn't complex.

encounters.frame: Tully is still upset about Saturday's match. Quillby is sorting his four versions of what happened.
encounters.prompt: Which of these is a compound sentence?
encounters.success: 'The Bombers led by thirty points at half-time' and 'they lost by a kick' are equals, joined by but.

options.text: The Bombers led by thirty points at half-time, but they lost by a kick.
Although the Bombers led by thirty points at half-time, they lost by a kick.
options.reason: 'Although the Bombers led by thirty points' can't stand alone, so this sentence is complex.

options.text: Despite leading by thirty points at half-time, the Bombers lost by a kick.
options.reason: Despite doesn't join two equal clauses. 'Despite leading by thirty points' can't stand on its own, so this isn't compound.

options.text: The Bombers' thirty-point lead at half-time had vanished by the final siren.
options.reason: There's only one clause here: the lead had vanished. Everything else is detail.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is reading the island news on his stream and calling this sentence simple.
encounters.text: Since the bridge collapsed during the storm, the ferry has been the only way across the river.
encounters.prompt: Which is the best description of this sentence?
encounters.success: Complex. 'Since the bridge collapsed during the storm' has its own doer and verb, but it can't stand alone.

options.text: complex: 'since the bridge collapsed during the storm' depends on the part that can stand alone
simple: since is about time, so it starts a phrase
options.reason: Since is about time, but 'the bridge collapsed' has its own doer and verb. So it's a clause.

options.text: compound: both parts could stand alone as sentences
options.reason: 'Since the bridge collapsed during the storm' can't stand alone. It leaves you waiting for the rest.

options.text: complex: 'during the storm' is the clause that can't stand alone
options.reason: 'During the storm' has no verb, so it's a phrase. The whole 'since' part can't stand alone.

encounters.frame: Zed's patch notes for his new game need labelling before release.
encounters.prompt: Match each line to the right label.
encounters.success: Long sentences can still be simple. What counts is how many clauses there are and whether they can stand alone.

items.text: Unless you collect every crystal, the final door stays locked.
items.reason: 'Unless you collect every crystal' can't stand alone, so the sentence is complex.

items.text: With every crystal in your backpack, the final door swings open.
items.reason: 'With every crystal in your backpack' has no verb. The only clause is 'the final door swings open'.

items.text: You can collect the crystals, or you can skip straight to the boss.
items.reason: Two clauses that could each stand alone, joined by or.

items.text: Players with a slow connection will notice a short delay.
items.reason: 'With a slow connection' is a phrase. There's one clause: players will notice.

items.text: The boss fight lags whenever more than four players join.
items.reason: 'Whenever more than four players join' has a doer and verb but can't stand alone, so it's complex.

items.text: The music has been remixed, and the lava now glows a brighter orange.
items.reason: Two equal clauses, each with its own verb, joined by and.

encounters.frame: Quillby is narrating a nature documentary about its cousin, the platypus.
encounters.prompt: Tap the only simple sentence.
encounters.success: The body-weight sentence has just one doer and one action, 'can eat'. That's simple.

parts.tap: Although platypuses look harmless, the males carry venomous spurs on their back legs.
parts.reason: 'Although platypuses look harmless' can't stand alone, so this is complex.

parts.tap: They hunt with their eyes shut, but they still find plenty of food.
parts.reason: Two equal clauses joined by but make this compound.

parts.tap: A single platypus can eat a fifth of its body weight in one night.
When the first stuffed platypus reached England, scientists thought it was a hoax.
parts.reason: 'When the first stuffed platypus reached England' can't stand alone, so this is complex.

encounters.frame: A concert review needs this sentence to be complex. Quillby has its nib ready.
encounters.prompt: Tap the joining word, then choose the replacement that makes one clause depend on the other.
encounters.success: Even though makes 'her top string had snapped' depend on the part that can stand alone. Now it's complex.

parts.reason: Finished is the verb in the part that can stand alone. Change the word that joins the clauses.
String is fine. Change the word that joins the clauses.
Snapped is the verb in the second clause. Change the word that joins the clauses.

options.reason: Yet joins two equal clauses, just like but, so the sentence stays compound.
However can't join two clauses after a comma. It makes neither part depend on the other.
And joins equals too, so the sentence stays compound. You'd also lose the contrast.

encounters.frame: The wreck divers' log is in pieces. Quillby needs a complex sentence from them.
encounters.prompt: Tap the pieces in order to make a complex sentence.
encounters.success: Although turns 'the water was barely above freezing' into a part that can't stand alone.

tiles: the water was barely above freezing.
accept: The divers kept exploring the wreck although the water was barely above freezing.
body.reason: Despite needs a noun after it, like 'despite the cold'. Here a whole clause follows, with its own verb.
